   310→        cli_command=cli_command,
   311→        original_report=report,
   312→        missing_ids=missing_ids,
   313→        duplicate_ids=duplicate_ids,
   314→    )
   315→    repair_prompt_file = prompts_dir / "reflect.repair.md"
   316→    repair_output_file = output_dir / "reflect.repair.raw.txt"
   317→    repair_log_file = logs_dir / "reflect.repair.log"
   318→    safe_write_text(repair_prompt_file, repair_prompt)
   319→    exit_code = run_triage_stage(
   320→        prompt=repair_prompt,
   321→        repo_root=repo_root,
   322→        output_file=repair_output_file,
   323→        log_file=repair_log_file,
   324→        timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   325→    )
   326→    append_run_log(f"stage-reflect-repair-done code={exit_code}")
   327→    if exit_code != 0:
   328→        return None, f"reflect_repair_failed_exit_{exit_code}"
   329→
   330→    repaired_report = _read_stage_output(repair_output_file)
   331→    if not repaired_report:
   332→        return None, "reflect_repair_empty_output"
   333→
   334→    _cited, missing_after, duplicates_after = _analyze_reflect_issue_accounting(
   335→        report=repaired_report,
   336→        valid_ids=set(getattr(si, "open_issues", {}).keys()),
   337→    )
   338→    if missing_after or duplicates_after:
   339→        return None, "reflect_repair_invalid"
   340→
   341→    print(colorize("  Reflect: repair pass fixed issue accounting.", "green"))
   342→    append_run_log("stage-reflect-repair-success")
   343→    return repaired_report, None
   344→
   345→
   346→def _execute_stage(
   347→    *,
   348→    stage: str,
   349→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   350→    services: TriageServices,
   351→    plan: dict,
   352→    si: dict,
   353→    prior_reports: dict[str, str],
   354→    repo_root: Path,
   355→    prompts_dir: Path,
   356→    output_dir: Path,
   357→    logs_dir: Path,
   358→    cli_command: str,
   359→    stage_start: float,
   360→    timeout_seconds: int,
   361→    dry_run: bool,
   362→    append_run_log,
   363→) -> tuple[str, dict]:
   364→    """Execute one stage and return (status, stage_result)."""
   365→    handler = _STAGE_HANDLERS.get(stage)
   366→    used_parallel = False
   367→    prompt_mode = handler.prompt_mode if handler is not None else "output_only"
   368→
   369→    preflight_ok, preflight_reason = _preflight_stage(
   370→        stage=stage,
   371→        plan=plan,
   372→        si=si,
   373→        append_run_log=append_run_log,
   374→    )
   375→    if not preflight_ok:
   376→        elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   377→        print(
   378→            colorize(
   379→                f"  Stage {stage}: blocked before launch ({preflight_reason}).",
   380→                "red",
   381→            )
   382→        )
   383→        return "failed", {
   384→            "status": "failed",
   385→            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   386→            "error": preflight_reason,
   387→        }
   388→
   389→    if handler and handler.run_parallel is not None:
   390→        parallel_ok, merged_report = handler.run_parallel(
   391→            si=si,
   392→            plan=plan,
   393→            repo_root=repo_root,
   394→            prompts_dir=prompts_dir,
   395→            output_dir=output_dir,
   396→            logs_dir=logs_dir,
   397→            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   398→            dry_run=dry_run,
   399→            append_run_log=append_run_log,
   400→        )
   401→        if parallel_ok is True and dry_run:
   402→            return "dry_run", {"status": "dry_run"}
   403→        if parallel_ok is True and merged_report:
   404→            if handler.record_report is not None:
   405→                handler.record_report(merged_report, args, services)
   406→            used_parallel = True
   407→        elif parallel_ok is False:
   408→            elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   409→            print(
   410→                colorize(f"  {stage.capitalize()}: parallel execution failed. Aborting.", "red")
   411→            )
   412→            append_run_log(
   413→                f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s reason=parallel_execution_failed"
   414→            )
   415→            return "failed", {"status": "failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed}
   416→
   417→    if not used_parallel:
   418→        prompt = build_stage_prompt(
   419→            stage,
   420→            si,
   421→            prior_reports,
   422→            repo_root=repo_root,
   423→            mode=prompt_mode,
   424→            cli_command=cli_command,
   425→        )
   426→
   427→        prompt_file = prompts_dir / f"{stage}.md"
   428→        safe_write_text(prompt_file, prompt)
   429→
   430→        if dry_run:
   431→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: prompt written to {prompt_file}", "cyan"))
   432→            print(colorize("  [dry-run] Would execute codex subprocess.", "dim"))
   433→            return "dry_run", {"status": "dry_run"}
   434→
   435→        print(colorize(f"\n  Stage {stage}: launching codex subprocess...", "bold"))
   436→        append_run_log(f"stage-subprocess-start stage={stage}")
   437→
   438→        output_file = output_dir / f"{stage}.raw.txt"
   439→        log_file = logs_dir / f"{stage}.log"
   440→
   441→        exit_code = run_triage_stage(
   442→            prompt=prompt,
   443→            repo_root=repo_root,
   444→            output_file=output_file,
   445→            log_file=log_file,
   446→            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   447→        )
   448→
   449→        elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   450→        append_run_log(
   451→            f"stage-subprocess-done stage={stage} code={exit_code} elapsed={elapsed}s"
   452→        )
   453→
   454→        if exit_code != 0:
   455→            print(
   456→                colorize(
   457→                    f"  Stage {stage}: codex subprocess failed (exit {exit_code}).", "red"
   458→                )
   459→            )
   460→            print(colorize(f"  Check log: {log_file}", "dim"))
   461→            print(colorize("  Re-run to resume (confirmed stages are skipped).", "dim"))
   462→            append_run_log(
   463→                f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s code={exit_code}"
   464→            )
   465→            return "failed", {
   466→                "status": "failed",
   467→                "exit_code": exit_code,
   468→                "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   469→            }
   470→
   471→        if handler and handler.record_report is not None:
   472→            report = _read_stage_output(output_file)
   473→            if report:
   474→                if stage == "reflect":
   475→                    report, repair_error = _repair_reflect_report_if_needed(
   476→                        report=report,
   477→                        si=si,
   478→                        prior_reports=prior_reports,
   479→                        repo_root=repo_root,
   480→                        prompts_dir=prompts_dir,
   481→                        output_dir=output_dir,
   482→                        logs_dir=logs_dir,
   483→                        cli_command=cli_command,
   484→                        timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   485→                        append_run_log=append_run_log,
   486→                    )
   487→                    if repair_error:
   488→                        print(
   489→                            colorize(
   490→                                f"  Stage {stage}: repair failed ({repair_error}).",
   491→                                "red",
   492→                            )
   493→                        )
   494→                        append_run_log(
   495→                            f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s reason={repair_error}"
   496→                        )
   497→                        return "failed", {
   498→                            "status": "failed",
   499→                            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   500→                            "error": repair_error,
   501→                        }
   502→                    if not report:
   503→                        append_run_log(
   504→                            f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s reason=reflect_repair_no_report"
   505→                        )
   506→                        return "failed", {
   507→                            "status": "failed",
   508→                            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   509→                            "error": "reflect_repair_no_report",
   510→                        }
   511→                handler.record_report(report, args, services)
   512→                plan_after_record = services.load_plan()
   513→                if not _stage_report_recorded(plan_after_record, stage):
   514→                    print(
   515→                        colorize(
   516→                            f"  Stage {stage}: handler completed but did not persist the stage.",
   517→                            "red",
   518→                        )
   519→                    )
   520→                    append_run_log(
   521→                        f"stage-record-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s reason=stage_not_recorded"
   522→                    )
   523→                    return "failed", {
   524→                        "status": "failed",
   525→                        "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   526→                        "error": "stage_not_recorded",
   527→                    }
   528→                append_run_log(
   529→                    f"stage-recorded stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s mode=orchestrator"
   530→                )
   531→            else:
   532→                print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: output file was empty after subprocess.", "red"))
   533→                append_run_log(
   534→                    f"stage-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s reason=empty_stage_output"
   535→                )
   536→                return "failed", {
   537→                    "status": "failed",
   538→                    "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   539→                    "error": "empty_stage_output",
   540→                }
   541→
   542→    return "ready", {}
   543→
   544→
   545→def _validate_and_confirm_stage(
   546→    *,
   547→    stage: str,
   548→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   549→    services: TriageServices,
   550→    si: dict,
   551→    state,
   552→    repo_root: Path,
   553→    stage_start: float,
   554→    append_run_log,
   555→) -> tuple[bool, dict, str]:
   556→    """Run shared stage validation + confirmation flow."""
   557→    plan = services.load_plan()
   558→
   559→    ok, error_msg = validate_stage(stage, plan, state, repo_root, triage_input=si)
   560→    if not ok:
   561→        elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   562→        print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: validation failed: {error_msg}", "red"))
   563→        print(colorize("  Re-run to resume.", "dim"))
   564→        append_run_log(
   565→            f"stage-validation-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s error={error_msg}"
   566→        )
   567→        return (
   568→            False,
   569→            {
   570→                "status": "validation_failed",
   571→                "elapsed_seconds": elapsed,
   572→                "error": error_msg,
   573→            },
   574→            "",
   575→        )
   576→
   577→    attestation = build_auto_attestation(stage, plan, si)
   578→    confirm_args = argparse.Namespace(
   579→        confirm=stage,
   580→        attestation=attestation,
   581→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   582→    )
   583→
   584→    from ..confirmations_router import cmd_confirm_stage
   585→
   586→    cmd_confirm_stage(confirm_args, services=services)
   587→
   588→    plan = services.load_plan()
   589→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   590→    stages_data = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   591→    elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - stage_start)
   592→    if stage in stages_data and stages_data[stage].get("confirmed_at"):
   593→        print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: confirmed ({elapsed}s).", "green"))
   594→        append_run_log(f"stage-confirmed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s")
   595→        report = stages_data.get(stage, {}).get("report", "")
   596→        return (
   597→            True,
   598→            {"status": "confirmed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   599→            report,
   600→        )
   601→
   602→    print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: auto-confirmation did not take effect.", "red"))
   603→    print(colorize("  Re-run to resume.", "dim"))
   604→    append_run_log(f"stage-confirm-failed stage={stage} elapsed={elapsed}s")
   605→    return (
   606→        False,
   607→        {"status": "confirm_failed", "elapsed_seconds": elapsed},
   608→        "",
   609→    )
   610→
   611→
   612→def _build_completion_strategy(stages_data: dict[str, dict]) -> str:
   613→    strategy_parts: list[str] = []
   614→    for stage in STAGES:
   615→        report = stages_data.get(stage, {}).get("report", "")
   616→        if report:
   617→            strategy_parts.append(f"[{stage}] {report[:200]}")
   618→    strategy = " ".join(strategy_parts)
   619→    if len(strategy) < 200:
   620→        strategy = strategy + " " + "Automated triage via codex subagent pipeline. " * 3
   621→    return strategy
   622→
   623→
   624→def _complete_pipeline(
   625→    *,
   626→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   627→    services: TriageServices,
   628→    plan: dict,
   629→    strategy: str,
   630→    triage_input: dict,
   631→) -> bool:
   632→    """Run the triage completion coordinator and report success."""
   633→    completed_before = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("last_completed_at")
   634→
   635→    print(colorize("\n  Completing triage...", "bold"))
   636→
   637→    attestation = build_auto_attestation("sense-check", plan, triage_input)
   638→    complete_args = argparse.Namespace(
   639→        complete=True,
   640→        strategy=strategy[:2000],
   641→        attestation=attestation,
   642→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   643→    )
   644→
   645→    from ..stage_completion_commands import _cmd_triage_complete
   646→
   647→    _cmd_triage_complete(complete_args, services=services)
   648→
   649→    completed_after = (
   650→        services.load_plan().get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("last_completed_at")
   651→    )
   652→    return bool(completed_after and completed_after != completed_before)
   653→
   654→
   655→def run_codex_pipeline(
   656→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   657→    *,
   658→    stages_to_run: list[str],
   659→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   660→) -> None:
   661→    """Run triage stages via Codex subprocesses (automated pipeline)."""
   662→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   663→    timeout_seconds = int(getattr(args, "stage_timeout_seconds", 1800) or 1800)
   664→    dry_run = bool(getattr(args, "dry_run", False))
   665→
   666→    repo_root = get_project_root()
   667→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   668→    ensure_triage_started(plan, resolved_services, runner="codex")
   669→
   670→    stamp = run_stamp()
   671→    desloppify_dir = repo_root / ".desloppify"
   672→    run_dir = desloppify_dir / "triage_runs" / stamp
   673→    prompts_dir = run_dir / "prompts"
   674→    output_dir = run_dir / "output"
   675→    logs_dir = run_dir / "logs"
   676→    for d in (prompts_dir, output_dir, logs_dir):
   677→        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   678→
   679→    run_log_path = run_dir / "run.log"
   680→    append_run_log = make_run_log_writer(run_log_path)
   681→    cli_helper = _write_desloppify_cli_helper(run_dir)
   682→    append_run_log(
   683→        f"run-start runner=codex stages={','.join(stages_to_run)} "
   684→        f"timeout={timeout_seconds}s dry_run={dry_run}"
   685→    )
   686→
   687→    print(colorize(f"  Run artifacts: {run_dir}", "dim"))
   688→    print(colorize(f"  Live run log:  {run_log_path}", "dim"))
   689→    print(colorize(f"  CLI helper:    {cli_helper}", "dim"))
   690→
   691→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   692→    state = runtime.state
   693→
   694→    prior_reports = _load_prior_reports_from_plan(plan)
   695→    stage_results: dict[str, dict] = {}
   696→    pipeline_start = time.monotonic()
   697→
   698→    for stage in stages_to_run:
   699→        plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   700→        meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   701→        stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   702→
   703→        if stage in stages and stages[stage].get("confirmed_at"):
   704→            print(colorize(f"  Stage {stage}: already confirmed, skipping.", "green"))
   705→            append_run_log(f"stage-skip stage={stage} reason=already_confirmed")
   706→            stage_results[stage] = {"status": "skipped"}
   707→            report = stages[stage].get("report", "")
   708→            if report:
   709→                prior_reports[stage] = report
   710→            continue
   711→
   712→        stage_start = time.monotonic()
   713→        append_run_log(f"stage-start stage={stage}")
   714→
   715→        si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   716→        exec_status, exec_result = _execute_stage(
   717→            stage=stage,
   718→            args=args,
   719→            services=resolved_services,
   720→            plan=plan,
   721→            si=si,
   722→            prior_reports=prior_reports,
   723→            repo_root=repo_root,
   724→            prompts_dir=prompts_dir,
   725→            output_dir=output_dir,
   726→            logs_dir=logs_dir,
   727→            cli_command=str(cli_helper),
   728→            stage_start=stage_start,
   729→            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
   730→            dry_run=dry_run,
   731→            append_run_log=append_run_log,
   732→        )
   733→        if exec_status == "dry_run":
   734→            stage_results[stage] = exec_result
   735→            continue
   736→        if exec_status == "failed":
   737→            stage_results[stage] = exec_result
   738→            write_triage_run_summary(
   739→                run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log
   740→            )
   741→            raise CommandError(
   742→                f"triage stage failed: {stage}. See {run_dir / 'run_summary.json'}",
   743→                exit_code=1,
   744→            )
   745→
   746→        confirmed, confirm_result, report = _validate_and_confirm_stage(
   747→            stage=stage,
   748→            args=args,
   749→            services=resolved_services,
   750→            si=si,
   751→            state=state,
   752→            repo_root=repo_root,
   753→            stage_start=stage_start,
   754→            append_run_log=append_run_log,
   755→        )
   756→        stage_results[stage] = confirm_result
   757→        if not confirmed:
   758→            write_triage_run_summary(
   759→                run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log
   760→            )
   761→            raise CommandError(
   762→                f"triage stage validation failed: {stage}. See {run_dir / 'run_summary.json'}",
   763→                exit_code=1,
   764→            )
   765→        if report:
   766→            prior_reports[stage] = report
   767→
   768→    if dry_run:
   769→        print(colorize("\n  [dry-run] All prompts generated. No stages executed.", "cyan"))
   770→        write_triage_run_summary(run_dir, stamp, stages_to_run, stage_results, append_run_log)
   771→        return
   772→
   773→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   774→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   775→    stages_data = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   776→
   777→    strategy = _build_completion_strategy(stages_data)
   778→
   779→    should_auto_complete = (
   780→        _is_full_stage_run(stages_to_run)
   781→        and _all_stage_results_successful(
   782→            stages_to_run=stages_to_run,
   783→            stage_results=stage_results,
   784→        )
   785→    )
   786→    if not should_auto_complete:
   787→        total_elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - pipeline_start)
   788→        _print_not_finalized_message("partial stage run")
   789→        append_run_log(f"run-finished elapsed={total_elapsed}s finalized=false reason=partial_stage_run")
   790→        write_triage_run_summary(
   791→            run_dir,
   792→            stamp,
   793→            stages_to_run,
   794→            stage_results,
   795→            append_run_log,
   796→            finalized=False,
   797→            finalization_reason="partial_stage_run",
   798→        )
   799→        return
   800→
   801→    completed = _complete_pipeline(
   802→        args=args,
   803→        services=resolved_services,
   804→        plan=plan,
   805→        strategy=strategy,
   806→        triage_input=si,
   807→    )
   808→    total_elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - pipeline_start)
   809→    if not completed:
   810→        _print_not_finalized_message("completion command blocked")
   811→        append_run_log(
   812→            f"run-finished elapsed={total_elapsed}s finalized=false reason=completion_blocked"
   813→        )
   814→        write_triage_run_summary(
   815→            run_dir,
   816→            stamp,
   817→            stages_to_run,
   818→            stage_results,
   819→            append_run_log,
   820→            finalized=False,
   821→            finalization_reason="completion_blocked",
   822→        )
   823→        return
   824→
   825→    print(colorize(f"\n  Triage pipeline complete ({total_elapsed}s).", "green"))
   826→    append_run_log(f"run-finished elapsed={total_elapsed}s finalized=true")
   827→    write_triage_run_summary(
   828→        run_dir,
   829→        stamp,
   830→        stages_to_run,
   831→        stage_results,
   832→        append_run_log,
   833→        finalized=True,
   834→    )
   835→
   836→
   837→def write_triage_run_summary(
   838→    run_dir: Path,
   839→    stamp: str,
   840→    stages: list[str],
   841→    stage_results: dict[str, dict],
   842→    append_run_log,
   843→    *,
   844→    finalized: bool | None = None,
   845→    finalization_reason: str | None = None,
   846→) -> None:
   847→    """Write a run_summary.json with per-stage results."""
   848→    summary = {
   849→        "created_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
   850→        "run_stamp": stamp,
   851→        "runner": "codex",
   852→        "stages_requested": stages,
   853→        "stage_results": stage_results,
   854→        "run_dir": str(run_dir),
   855→    }
   856→    if finalized is not None:
   857→        summary["finalized"] = finalized
   858→    if finalization_reason:
   859→        summary["finalization_reason"] = finalization_reason
   860→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   861→    safe_write_text(summary_path, json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n")
   862→    print(colorize(f"  Run summary: {summary_path}", "dim"))
   863→    append_run_log(f"run-summary {summary_path}")
   864→
   865→
   866→__all__ = ["run_codex_pipeline"]
   867→

1→"""update-skill command: install or update the desloppify skill document."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import urllib.error
     7→import urllib.request
     8→
     9→from desloppify.app.skill_docs import (
    10→    SKILL_BEGIN,
    11→    SKILL_END,
    12→    SKILL_TARGETS,
    13→    SKILL_VERSION,
    14→    SKILL_VERSION_RE,
    15→    SkillInstall,
    16→    find_installed_skill,
    17→)

    22→_RAW_BASE = (
    23→    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/peteromallet/desloppify/main/docs"
    24→)
    25→
    26→
    27→def _download(filename: str) -> str:
    28→    """Download a file from the desloppify docs directory on GitHub."""
    29→    url = f"{_RAW_BASE}/{filename}"
    30→    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as resp:  # noqa: S310
    31→        return resp.read().decode("utf-8")
    32→
    33→
    34→def _build_section(skill_content: str, overlay_content: str | None) -> str:
    35→    """Assemble the complete skill section from downloaded parts."""
    36→    parts = [skill_content.rstrip()]
    37→    if overlay_content:
    38→        parts.append(overlay_content.rstrip())
    39→    return "\n\n".join(parts) + "\n"
    40→
    41→
    42→# Interfaces whose skill systems parse YAML frontmatter and require ``---``
    43→# to appear on the very first line of the file.
    44→_FRONTMATTER_FIRST_INTERFACES = frozenset({"amp", "codex"})
    45→
    46→
    47→def _ensure_frontmatter_first(content: str) -> str:
    48→    """Move YAML frontmatter to the top if HTML comments precede it.
    49→
    50→    Some skill systems (e.g. AMP) require ``---`` on line 1 for frontmatter
    51→    parsing.  SKILL.md ships with ``<!-- desloppify-begin -->`` and a version
    52→    comment before the ``---`` block.  This function relocates those HTML
    53→    comment lines to just after the closing ``---``.
    54→    """
    55→    lines = content.split("\n")
    56→
    57→    # Find the opening ``---``.
    58→    fm_start = None
    59→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
    60→        if line.strip() == "---":
    61→            fm_start = i
    62→            break
    63→    if fm_start is None or fm_start == 0:
    64→        return content  # already fine or no frontmatter
    65→
    66→    # Collect the HTML-comment lines that precede the frontmatter.
    67→    prefix_lines = lines[:fm_start]
    68→
    69→    # Find the closing ``---``.
    70→    fm_end = None
    71→    for i, line in enumerate(lines[fm_start + 1 :], fm_start + 1):
    72→        if line.strip() == "---":
    73→            fm_end = i
    74→            break
    75→    if fm_end is None:
    76→        return content  # malformed frontmatter, leave untouched
    77→
    78→    # Reassemble: frontmatter first, then the prefix lines, then the rest.
    79→    reordered = (
    80→        lines[fm_start : fm_end + 1]
    81→        + prefix_lines
    82→        + lines[fm_end + 1 :]
    83→    )
    84→    return "\n".join(reordered)
    85→
    86→
    87→def _replace_section(file_content: str, new_section: str) -> str:
    88→    """Replace the desloppify section in a shared file, preserving surrounding content.
    89→
    90→    Uses first ``<!-- desloppify-begin -->`` and last ``<!-- desloppify-end -->``
    91→    so the overlay (which also has an end marker) is captured correctly.
    92→    """
    93→    begin = file_content.find(SKILL_BEGIN)
    94→    end = file_content.rfind(SKILL_END)
    95→    if begin == -1 or end == -1:
    96→        # No section markers — append (first install into existing shared file).
    97→        return file_content.rstrip() + "\n\n" + new_section
    98→
    99→    before = file_content[:begin]
   100→    after = file_content[end + len(SKILL_END):]
   101→    before = before.rstrip() + "\n\n" if before.strip() else ""
   102→    after = "\n" + after.lstrip("\n") if after.strip() else "\n"
   103→    return before + new_section + after
   104→
   105→
   106→def resolve_interface(
   107→    explicit: str | None = None,
   108→    install: SkillInstall | None = None,
   109→) -> str | None:
   110→    """Resolve which interface to update.
   111→
   112→    Uses the explicit argument if given, otherwise infers from an existing
   113→    install's overlay marker or file path.
   114→    """
   115→    if explicit:
   116→        return explicit.lower()
   117→
   118→    if install is None:
   119→        install = find_installed_skill()
   120→    if not install:
   121→        return None
   122→
   123→    if install.overlay:
   124→        return install.overlay.lower()
   125→
   126→    for name, (target, _overlay, _ded) in SKILL_TARGETS.items():
   127→        if target == install.rel_path:
   128→            return name
   129→    return None
   130→
   131→
   132→def update_installed_skill(interface: str) -> bool:
   133→    """Download and install the skill document for the given interface.
   134→
   135→    Returns True on success, False on failure. Prints status messages.
   136→    """
   137→    target_rel, overlay_name, dedicated = SKILL_TARGETS[interface]
   138→    target_path = get_project_root() / target_rel
   139→
   140→    print(colorize(f"Downloading skill document ({interface})...", "dim"))
   141→    try:
   142→        skill_content = _download("SKILL.md")
   143→        overlay_content = _download(f"{overlay_name}.md") if overlay_name else None
   144→    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError) as exc:
   145→        print(colorize(f"Download failed: {exc}", "red"))
   146→        return False
   147→
   148→    if "desloppify-skill-version" not in skill_content:
   149→        print(colorize("Downloaded content doesn't look like a skill document.", "red"))
   150→        return False
   151→
   152→    new_section = _build_section(skill_content, overlay_content)
   153→    if interface in _FRONTMATTER_FIRST_INTERFACES:
   154→        new_section = _ensure_frontmatter_first(new_section)
   155→
   156→    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   157→    if dedicated:
   158→        result = new_section
   159→    elif target_path.is_file():
   160→        existing = target_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   161→        result = _replace_section(existing, new_section)
   162→    else:
   163→        result = new_section
   164→
   165→    safe_write_text(target_path, result)
   166→
   167→    version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(new_section)
   168→    version = version_match.group(1) if version_match else "?"
   169→    print(
   170→        colorize(
   171→            f"Updated {target_rel} (v{version}, tool expects v{SKILL_VERSION})",
   172→            "green",
   173→        )
   174→    )
   175→    return True
   176→
   177→
   178→def cmd_update_skill(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   179→    """Install or update the desloppify skill document."""
   180→    interface = resolve_interface(getattr(args, "interface", None))
   181→
   182→    if not interface:
   183→        print(colorize("No installed skill document found.", "yellow"))
   184→        print()
   185→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   186→        print(f"Install with: desloppify update-skill <{names}>")
   187→        return
   188→
   189→    if interface not in SKILL_TARGETS:
   190→        names = ", ".join(sorted(SKILL_TARGETS))
   191→        print(colorize(f"Unknown interface '{interface}'.", "red"))
   192→        print(f"Available: {names}")
   193→        return
   194→
   195→    update_installed_skill(interface)
   196→

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through issues, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from collections.abc import Callable
    12→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    13→from enum import Enum
    14→
    15→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    16→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    17→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    19→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    20→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    21→)
    22→
    23→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    24→
    25→
    26→class Zone(str, Enum):
    27→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    28→
    29→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    30→    TEST = "test"
    31→    CONFIG = "config"
    32→    GENERATED = "generated"
    33→    SCRIPT = "script"
    34→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    35→
    36→
    37→# Zones excluded from the health score
    38→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    39→
    40→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (issues store zone as string)
    41→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    42→
    43→
    44→@dataclass
    45→class ZoneRule:
    46→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    47→
    48→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    49→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    50→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    51→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    52→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    53→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    54→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    55→    """
    56→
    57→    zone: Zone
    58→    patterns: list[str]
    59→
    60→
    61→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    62→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    63→
    64→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    65→    """
    66→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    67→
    68→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    69→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    70→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    71→
    72→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    73→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    74→        return pattern in basename
    75→
    76→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    77→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    78→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    79→
    80→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    81→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    82→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    83→
    84→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    85→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    86→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    87→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    88→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    89→            return basename == pattern
    90→
    91→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    92→    return pattern in rel_path
    93→
    94→
    95→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    96→
    97→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   101→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   102→]
   103→
   104→
   105→def classify_file(
   106→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   107→) -> Zone:
   108→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   109→    if overrides:
   110→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   111→        if override:
   112→            try:
   113→                return Zone(override)
   114→            except ValueError as exc:
   115→                log_best_effort_failure(
   116→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   117→                )
   118→    for rule in rules:
   119→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   120→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   121→                return rule.zone
   122→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   123→
   124→
   125→class FileZoneMap:
   126→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   127→
   128→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   129→    """
   130→
   131→    def __init__(
   132→        self,
   133→        files: list[str],
   134→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   135→        rel_fn: Callable[[str], str] | None = None,
   136→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   137→    ):
   138→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   139→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   140→        self._rel_map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   141→        self._rel_fn = rel_fn
   142→        self._overrides = overrides
   143→        for file_path in files:
   144→            rel_path = rel_fn(file_path) if rel_fn else file_path
   145→            zone = classify_file(rel_path, rules, overrides)
   146→            self._map[file_path] = zone
   147→            self._rel_map[rel_path] = zone
   148→
   149→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   150→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   151→        direct = self._map.get(path)
   152→        if direct is not None:
   153→            return direct
   154→
   155→        rel_direct = self._rel_map.get(path)
   156→        if rel_direct is not None:
   157→            return rel_direct
   158→
   159→        if self._rel_fn is not None:
   160→            try:
   161→                rel_path = self._rel_fn(path)
   162→            except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError):
   163→                rel_path = path
   164→            rel_zone = self._rel_map.get(rel_path)
   165→            if rel_zone is not None:
   166→                return rel_zone
   167→
   168→        return Zone.PRODUCTION
   169→
   170→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   171→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   172→        zone_set = set(zones)
   173→        return [
   174→            file_path
   175→            for file_path in files
   176→            if self._map.get(file_path, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set
   177→        ]
   178→
   179→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   180→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   181→        zone_set = set(zones)
   182→        return [
   183→            file_path
   184→            for file_path in files
   185→            if self._map.get(file_path, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set
   186→        ]
   187→
   188→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   189→        """Return file count per zone."""
   190→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   191→        for zone in self._map.values():
   192→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   193→        return counts
   194→
   195→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   196→        """Count files classified as production."""
   197→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   198→
   199→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   200→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   201→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   202→
   203→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   204→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   205→        return list(self._map.keys())
   206→
   207→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   208→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   209→        return list(self._map.items())
   210→
   211→
   212→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   213→
   214→
   215→@dataclass
   216→class ZonePolicy:
   217→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   218→
   219→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   220→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   221→    exclude_from_score: whether issues in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   222→    """
   223→
   224→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   225→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   226→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   227→
   228→
   229→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   230→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   231→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   232→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   233→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   234→        exclude_from_score=True,
   235→    ),
   236→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   237→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   238→        exclude_from_score=True,
   239→    ),
   240→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   241→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   242→        exclude_from_score=True,
   243→    ),
   244→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   245→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   246→        exclude_from_score=True,
   247→    ),
   248→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   249→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   250→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   251→    ),
   252→}
   253→
   254→
   255→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   256→
   257→
   258→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   259→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   260→
   261→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   262→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   263→    """
   264→    if zone_map is None:
   265→        return total
   266→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   267→
   268→
   269→def should_skip_issue(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   270→    """Check if a issue should be skipped based on zone policy.
   271→
   272→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   273→    """
   274→    if zone_map is None:
   275→        return False
   276→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   277→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   278→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   279→
   280→
   281→def filter_entries(
   282→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   283→) -> list[dict]:
   284→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   285→
   286→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   287→    the first element.
   288→    """
   289→    if zone_map is None:
   290→        return entries
   291→
   292→    def _get_path(entry):
   293→        val = entry[file_key]
   294→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   295→
   296→    return [
   297→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   298→    ]

    41→    """Clear all cycle state when --force-rescan is used.

    44→    workflow items, subjective dimensions, plan-start scores, and triage
    45→    metadata are all stale and must be removed.

    49→    if not synthetic and not plan.get("plan_start_scores"):
    50→        return False
    51→    for item in synthetic:
    52→        order.remove(item)
    53→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {}

   153→def _seed_plan_start_scores(plan: dict[str, object], state: state_mod.StateModel) -> bool:
   154→    """Set plan_start_scores when beginning a new queue cycle."""
   155→    existing = plan.get("plan_start_scores")
   156→    if existing and not isinstance(existing, dict):
   157→        return False
   158→    # Seed when empty OR when it's the reset sentinel ({"reset": True})
   159→    if existing and not existing.get("reset"):

   162→    if scores.strict is None:

   164→    plan["plan_start_scores"] = {

   166→        "overall": scores.overall,
   167→        "objective": scores.objective,
   168→        "verified": scores.verified,
   169→    }
   170→    # New cycle — clear the communicate-score sentinel so it can fire again.
   171→    plan.pop("previous_plan_start_scores", None)
   172→    # Record scan count at cycle start so gates can detect whether a new scan ran
   173→    plan["scan_count_at_plan_start"] = int(state.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)

   439→def _is_mid_cycle_scan(plan: dict[str, object], state: state_mod.StateModel) -> bool:

   441→
   442→    Extends ``is_mid_cycle`` (which checks ``plan_start_scores``) with an
   443→    additional queue-items guard — even if a cycle is nominally active, we
   444→    only skip destructive operations when work actually remains.
   445→
   446→    Mid-cycle scans (via --force-rescan or PHASE_TRANSITION gate) must NOT
   447→    regenerate clusters or inject triage stages — doing so wipes triage
   448→    state and reorders the queue, undoing prioritisation work.
   449→    """
   450→    if not is_mid_cycle(plan):
   451→        return False
   452→    order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   453→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   454→    return any(item not in skipped for item in order)

   463→    cycle_just_completed: bool,
   464→    force_rescan: bool = False,
   465→) -> bool:
   466→    """Run post-scan sync steps that require policy/cycle context.
   467→
   468→    When running mid-cycle (plan_start_scores set, queue non-empty) or
   469→    via --force-rescan, skip auto-clustering and triage injection.  These
   470→    steps regenerate queue structure and issue IDs, which wipes triage
   471→    state and reorders the queue.  They only run at cycle boundaries
   472→    (pre-flight / post-flight).
   473→    """
   474→    dirty = False
   475→    mid_cycle = _is_mid_cycle_scan(plan, state) or force_rescan
   476→
   477→    if _sync_stale_and_log(
   478→        plan,
   479→        state,
   480→        policy=policy,
   481→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   482→    ):
   483→        dirty = True
   484→    if not mid_cycle:
   485→        if _sync_auto_clusters_and_log(
   486→            plan,
   487→            state,
   488→            target_strict=target_strict,
   489→            policy=policy,
   490→            cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   491→        ):
   492→            dirty = True
   493→    else:
   494→        print(
   495→            colorize(
   496→                "  Plan: mid-cycle scan — skipping cluster regeneration to "
   497→                "preserve queue state.",
   498→                "dim",
   499→            )
   500→        )
   501→    if _sync_communicate_score_and_log(plan, state, policy=policy):
   502→        dirty = True
   503→    if _sync_create_plan_and_log(plan, state, policy=policy):
   504→        dirty = True
   505→    if _sync_triage_and_log(plan, state, policy=policy):
   506→        dirty = True
   507→    if not force_rescan:
   508→        if _sync_plan_start_scores_and_log(plan, state):
   509→            dirty = True
   510→        if _sync_postflight_scan_completion_and_log(plan, state):
   511→            dirty = True
   512→    return dirty
   513→
   514→
   515→def reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime: ScanRuntime) -> None:
   516→    """Reconcile plan queue metadata and stale subjective review dimensions."""
   517→    plan_path = runtime.state_path.parent / "plan.json" if runtime.state_path else None
   518→    try:
   519→        plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   520→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   521→        logger.warning("Plan reconciliation skipped (load failed): %s", exc)
   522→        return
   523→
   524→    force_rescan = getattr(runtime, "force_rescan", False)
   525→
   526→    # Force-rescan: clear all cycle state first.  The user explicitly chose
   527→    # to start over, so triage stages, workflow items, subjective dimensions,
   528→    # and plan-start scores from the old cycle are all stale.
   529→    dirty = _reset_cycle_for_force_rescan(plan) if force_rescan else False
   530→
   531→    dirty = _sync_post_scan_without_policy(plan=plan, state=runtime.state) or dirty
   532→
   533→    # Policy must be computed after the without-policy steps, which mutate
   534→    # plan (reconcile/prune) and state (unscored sync) before policy reads them.
   535→    target_strict, policy, cycle_just_completed = _subjective_policy_context(
   536→        runtime,
   537→        plan,
   538→    )
   539→    dirty = _sync_post_scan_with_policy(
   540→        plan=plan,
   541→        state=runtime.state,
   542→        target_strict=target_strict,
   543→        policy=policy,
   544→        cycle_just_completed=cycle_just_completed,
   545→        force_rescan=getattr(runtime, "force_rescan", False),
   546→    ) or dirty
   547→
   548→    if dirty:
   549→        try:
   550→            save_plan(plan, plan_path)
   551→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   552→            logger.warning("Plan reconciliation save failed: %s", exc)
   553→

   201→

   203→def _apply_assessment_reset(payload: dict, *, source: str, now: str) -> None:
   204→    """Apply a standard reset mutation to a single subjective assessment payload.
   205→
   206→    Sets score to 0.0, stamps assessed_at/reset_by/placeholder, and strips
   207→    any cached scoring artifacts (integrity_penalty, components,
   208→    component_scores) plus provisional-override markers.
   209→    """
   210→    payload["score"] = 0.0
   211→    payload["source"] = source
   212→    payload["assessed_at"] = now
   213→    payload["reset_by"] = source
   214→    payload["placeholder"] = True
   215→    payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   216→    payload.pop("components", None)
   217→    payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   218→    payload.pop("provisional_override", None)
   219→    payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   220→
   221→
   222→def _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   223→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   224→    *,
   225→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   226→) -> int:
   227→    """Reset known subjective dimensions to 0 so the next scan starts fresh."""
   228→    assessments = _state_subjective_assessments(state)
   229→
   230→    reset_keys = {
   231→        key.strip()
   232→        for key in assessments
   233→        if isinstance(key, str) and key.strip()
   234→    }
   235→    reset_keys.update(_subjective_reset_dimensions(lang_name=lang_name))
   236→
   237→    now = state_mod.utc_now()
   238→    source = "scan_reset_subjective"
   239→    for key in sorted(reset_keys):
   240→        payload = assessments.get(key)
   241→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   242→            _apply_assessment_reset(payload, source=source, now=now)
   243→            continue
   244→        assessments[key] = {
   245→            "score": 0.0,
   246→            "source": source,
   247→            "assessed_at": now,
   248→            "reset_by": source,
   249→            "placeholder": True,
   250→        }
   251→    return len(reset_keys)
   252→
   253→
   254→
   255→
   256→def prepare_scan_runtime(args: argparse.Namespace) -> ScanRuntime:
   257→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   258→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   259→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   260→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   261→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)
   262→    path = Path(args.path)
   263→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   264→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   265→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   266→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   267→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   268→            state,
   269→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   270→        )
   271→
   272→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   273→    profile = resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   274→    include_slow_effective = effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   275→
   276→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   277→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   278→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   279→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   280→
   281→    return ScanRuntime(
   282→        args=args,
   283→        state_path=state_file,
   284→        state=state,
   285→        path=path,
   286→        config=config,
   287→        lang=lang,
   288→        lang_label=f" ({lang.name})" if lang else "",
   289→        profile=profile,
   290→        effective_include_slow=include_slow_effective,
   291→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   292→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   293→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   294→        force_rescan=bool(getattr(args, "force_rescan", False)),
   295→    )
   296→
   297→
   298→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(
   299→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   300→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   301→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   302→    """Append stale exclude issues when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   303→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   304→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   305→        return issues
   306→
   307→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   308→    stale = audit_excluded_dirs(
   309→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, get_project_root()
   310→    )
   311→    if not stale:
   312→        return issues
   313→
   314→    augmented = list(issues)
   315→    augmented.extend(stale)
   316→    for stale_issue in stale:
   317→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_issue['summary']}", "dim"))
   318→    return augmented
   319→
   320→
   321→def _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   322→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   323→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   324→    *,
   325→    decay_scans: int,
   326→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   327→    """Append re-triage issues for stale/worsening wontfix debt."""
   328→    return _augment_stale_wontfix_impl(
   329→        issues,
   330→        state=runtime.state,
   331→        scan_path=runtime.path,
   332→        project_root=get_project_root(),
   333→        decay_scans=decay_scans,
   334→    )
   335→
   336→
   337→def run_scan_generation(
   338→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   339→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   340→    """Run detector pipeline and return issues, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   341→    enable_file_cache()
   342→    enable_parse_cache()
   343→    try:
   344→        issues, potentials = plan_mod.generate_issues(
   345→            runtime.path,
   346→            lang=runtime.lang,
   347→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   348→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   349→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   350→                profile=runtime.profile,
   351→            ),
   352→        )
   353→    finally:
   354→        disable_parse_cache()
   355→        disable_file_cache()
   356→
   357→    codebase_metrics = collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   358→    warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   359→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   360→    )
   361→    issues = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(issues, runtime)
   362→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   363→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   364→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   365→    )
   366→    issues, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   367→        issues,
   368→        runtime,
   369→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   370→    )
   371→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   372→    return issues, potentials, codebase_metrics
   373→
   374→
   375→def merge_scan_results(
   376→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   377→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   378→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   379→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   380→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   381→    """Merge issues into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   382→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   383→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   384→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   385→
   386→    if not path_changed:
   387→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   388→    else:
   389→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   390→    prev_dim_scores = (
   391→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   392→    )
   393→
   394→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   395→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   396→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   397→
   398→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config)
   399→
   400→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   401→        runtime.state,
   402→        issues,
   403→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   404→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   405→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   406→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   407→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   408→            potentials=potentials,
   409→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   410→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   411→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   412→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   413→        ),
   414→    )
   415→
   416→    expire_stale_holistic(
   417→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   418→    )
   419→    state_mod.save_state(
   420→        runtime.state,
   421→        runtime.state_path,
   422→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   423→    )
   424→
   425→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)
   426→    _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
   427→
   428→    return ScanMergeResult(
   429→        diff=diff,
   430→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   431→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   432→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   433→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   434→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   435→    )
   436→
   437→
   438→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   439→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   440→    config: dict[str, object],
   441→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   442→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden issue counters."""
   443→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   444→        state_mod.resolve_issue_noise_settings(config)
   445→    )
   446→    issues_by_id = _state_issues(state)
   447→    open_issues = [
   448→        issue
   449→        for issue in state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   450→            issues_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   451→        ).values()
   452→        if issue.get("status") == "open"
   453→    ]
   454→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_issue_noise_budget(
   455→        open_issues,
   456→        budget=noise_budget,
   457→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   458→    )
   459→
   460→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   461→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   462→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   463→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   464→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   465→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   466→    )
   467→
   468→
   469→def persist_reminder_history(
   470→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   471→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   472→) -> None:
   473→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   474→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   475→        return
   476→
   477→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   478→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config)
   479→    state_mod.save_state(
   480→        runtime.state,
   481→        runtime.state_path,
   482→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   483→    )
   484→
   485→
   486→__all__ = [
   487→    "ScanStateContractError",
   488→    "ScanMergeResult",
   489→    "ScanNoiseSnapshot",
   490→    "ScanRuntime",
   491→    "merge_scan_results",
   492→    "persist_reminder_history",
   493→    "prepare_scan_runtime",
   494→    "resolve_noise_snapshot",
   495→    "run_scan_generation",
   496→]

    59→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    60→class NormalizedBatchIssue:
    61→    """Typed internal issue contract for normalized batch payloads."""
    62→
    63→    dimension: str
    64→    identifier: str
    65→    summary: str
    66→    confidence: str
    67→    suggestion: str
    68→    related_files: list[str]
    69→    evidence: list[str]
    70→    impact_scope: str

    72→    reasoning: str = ""
    73→    evidence_lines: list[int] | None = None
    74→
    75→    def to_payload(self) -> BatchIssuePayload:
    76→        payload = cast(
    77→            BatchIssuePayload,
    78→            {
    79→                "dimension": self.dimension,
    80→                "identifier": self.identifier,
    81→                "summary": self.summary,
    82→                "confidence": self.confidence,
    83→                "suggestion": self.suggestion,
    84→                "related_files": list(self.related_files),
    85→                "evidence": list(self.evidence),
    86→                "impact_scope": self.impact_scope,
    87→                "fix_scope": self.fix_scope,
    88→            },
    89→        )
    90→        if self.reasoning:
    91→            payload["reasoning"] = self.reasoning
    92→        if self.evidence_lines:
    93→            payload["evidence_lines"] = list(self.evidence_lines)
    94→        return payload
    95→

   166→
   167→    batch_positions = {batch_idx: pos + 1 for pos, batch_idx in enumerate(selected_indexes)}

   186→    report_progress = build_progress_reporter(

   199→    summary_config = BatchRunSummaryConfig(

   266→    }
   267→
   268→
   269→def execute_batch_run(*, prepared: dict[str, Any], deps: BatchRunDeps) -> dict[str, Any]:
   270→    """Execute prepared tasks and return reconciliation outputs."""
   271→    selected_indexes = prepared["selected_indexes"]
   272→    tasks = build_batch_tasks(
   273→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   274→        prompt_files=prepared["prompt_files"],
   275→        output_files=prepared["output_files"],
   276→        log_files=prepared["log_files"],
   277→        project_root=prepared["project_root"],
   278→        run_codex_batch_fn=deps.run_codex_batch_fn,
   279→    )
   280→    try:
   281→        execution_failures = deps.execute_batches_fn(
   282→            tasks=tasks,
   283→            options=BatchExecutionOptions(
   284→                run_parallel=prepared["run_parallel"],
   285→                max_parallel_workers=prepared["max_parallel_batches"],
   286→                heartbeat_seconds=prepared["heartbeat_seconds"],
   287→            ),
   288→            progress_fn=prepared["report_progress"],
   289→            error_log_fn=prepared["record_issue"],
   290→        )
   291→    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   292→        mark_interrupted_batches(
   293→            selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   294→            batch_status=prepared["batch_status"],
   295→            batch_positions=prepared["batch_positions"],
   296→        )
   297→        prepared["write_run_summary"](
   298→            successful_batches=[],
   299→            failed_batches=[],
   300→            interrupted=True,
   301→            interruption_reason="keyboard_interrupt",
   302→        )
   303→        prepared["append_run_log"]("run-interrupted reason=keyboard_interrupt")
   304→        raise SystemExit(130) from None
   305→
   306→    batch_results, successful_indexes, failures, failure_set = collect_and_reconcile_results(
   307→        collect_batch_results_fn=deps.collect_batch_results_fn,
   308→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   309→        execution_failures=execution_failures,
   310→        output_files=prepared["output_files"],
   311→        packet=prepared["packet"],
   312→        batch_positions=prepared["batch_positions"],
   313→        batch_status=prepared["batch_status"],
   314→        colorize_fn=deps.colorize_fn,
   315→    )
   316→    prepared["write_run_summary"](
   317→        successful_batches=[idx + 1 for idx in successful_indexes],
   318→        failed_batches=[idx + 1 for idx in sorted(failure_set)],
   319→    )
   320→
   321→    if failures and (not prepared["allow_partial"] or not batch_results):
   322→        prepared["append_run_log"](
   323→            f"run-finished failures={[idx + 1 for idx in sorted(failure_set)]} mode=exit"
   324→        )
   325→        deps.print_failures_and_raise_fn(
   326→            failures=failures,
   327→            packet_path=prepared["immutable_packet_path"],
   328→            logs_dir=prepared["logs_dir"],
   329→            colorize_fn=deps.colorize_fn,
   330→        )
   331→    elif failures:
   332→        print(
   333→            deps.colorize_fn(
   334→                "  Partial completion enabled: importing successful batches and keeping failed batches open.",
   335→                "yellow",
   336→            )
   337→        )
   338→        deps.print_failures_fn(
   339→            failures=failures,
   340→            packet_path=prepared["immutable_packet_path"],
   341→            logs_dir=prepared["logs_dir"],
   342→            colorize_fn=deps.colorize_fn,
   343→        )
   344→        prepared["append_run_log"](
   345→            "run-partial "
   346→            f"successful={[idx + 1 for idx in successful_indexes]} "
   347→            f"failed={[idx + 1 for idx in sorted(failure_set)]}"
   348→        )
   349→
   350→    return {
   351→        "batch_results": batch_results,
   352→        "successful_indexes": successful_indexes,
   353→        "failure_set": failure_set,
   354→    }
   355→
   356→
   357→def merge_and_import_batch_run(
   358→    *,
   359→    prepared: dict[str, Any],
   360→    executed: dict[str, Any],
   361→    state_file,
   362→    deps: BatchRunDeps,
   363→) -> None:
   364→    """Merge successful batch results and import final holistic output."""
   365→    merged_path, missing_after_import = merge_and_write_results(
   366→        merge_batch_results_fn=deps.merge_batch_results_fn,
   367→        build_import_provenance_fn=deps.build_import_provenance_fn,
   368→        batch_results=executed["batch_results"],
   369→        batches=prepared["batches"],
   370→        successful_indexes=executed["successful_indexes"],
   371→        packet=prepared["packet"],
   372→        packet_dimensions=prepared["packet_dimensions"],
   373→        scored_dimensions=prepared["scored_dimensions"],
   374→        scan_path=prepared["scan_path"],
   375→        runner=prepared["runner"],
   376→        prompt_packet_path=prepared["prompt_packet_path"],
   377→        stamp=prepared["stamp"],
   378→        run_dir=prepared["run_dir"],
   379→        safe_write_text_fn=deps.safe_write_text_fn,
   380→        colorize_fn=deps.colorize_fn,
   381→    )
   382→    enforce_import_coverage(
   383→        missing_after_import=missing_after_import,
   384→        packet_dimensions=prepared["packet_dimensions"],
   385→        allow_partial=prepared["allow_partial"],
   386→        scan_path=prepared["scan_path"],
   387→        colorize_fn=deps.colorize_fn,
   388→    )
   389→    import_and_finalize(
   390→        do_import_fn=deps.do_import_fn,
   391→        run_followup_scan_fn=deps.run_followup_scan_fn,
   392→        merged_path=merged_path,
   393→        state=prepared["state"],
   394→        lang=prepared["lang"],
   395→        state_file=state_file,
   396→        config=prepared["config"],
   397→        allow_partial=prepared["allow_partial"],
   398→        successful_indexes=executed["successful_indexes"],
   399→        failure_set=executed["failure_set"],
   400→        append_run_log=prepared["append_run_log"],
   401→        args=prepared["args"],
   402→    )
   403→
   404→
   405→__all__ = ["execute_batch_run", "merge_and_import_batch_run", "prepare_batch_run"]
   406→

    23→def _payload_size_bytes(payload: dict) -> int:
    24→    """Return UTF-8 byte size for a JSON-serializable payload."""
    25→    return len(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, default=json_default).encode("utf-8"))
    26→
    27→
    28→def _truncate_text(value: object, *, limit: int | None = None) -> object:
    29→    """Return text truncated to a fixed character budget."""
    30→    if not isinstance(value, str):
    31→        return value
    32→    limit_value = QUERY_TEXT_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
    33→    if len(value) <= limit_value:
    34→        return value
    35→    return value[: limit_value - 1] + "…"
    36→
    37→
    38→def _lightweight_item(item: object) -> object:
    39→    """Return a lighter-weight queue item safe for query payload persistence."""
    40→    if not isinstance(item, dict):
    41→        return item
    42→
    43→    light = dict(item)
    44→    light["summary"] = _truncate_text(light.get("summary"))
    45→
    46→    detail = light.get("detail")
    47→    if isinstance(detail, dict):
    48→        compact_detail: dict = {}
    49→        for key, value in detail.items():
    50→            if isinstance(value, str):
    51→                compact_detail[key] = _truncate_text(value, limit=200)
    52→            elif isinstance(value, list):
    53→                compact_detail[key] = value[:20]
    54→            elif isinstance(value, dict):
    55→                compact_detail[key] = {"truncated": True, "keys": len(value)}
    56→            else:
    57→                compact_detail[key] = value
    58→        light["detail"] = compact_detail
    59→
    60→    if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
    61→        members = light.get("members")
    62→        if isinstance(members, list) and len(members) > QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT:
    63→            light["members"] = members[:QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT]
    64→            light["members_truncated"] = True
    65→            light["members_sample_limit"] = QUERY_CLUSTER_MEMBER_LIMIT
    66→
    67→    return light
    68→
    69→
    70→def _minimal_payload(payload: dict, *, max_bytes: int) -> dict:
    71→    """Build a minimal fallback payload when budget cannot be met."""
    72→    minimal: dict = {
    73→        "command": payload.get("command"),
    74→        "queue": payload.get("queue", {}),
    75→        "overall_score": payload.get("overall_score"),

    86→            sample_items.append(

    91→                    "file": item.get("file"),

    97→    if "config" in payload:

    99→    if "config_error" in payload:
   100→        minimal["config_error"] = payload["config_error"]
   101→

    16→def _compute_fp_rates(issues: dict) -> dict[tuple[str, str], float]:
    17→    """Compute false_positive rate per (detector, zone) from historical issues."""
    18→    counts: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, int]] = {}
    19→    for issue in issues.values():
    20→        detector = issue.get("detector", "unknown")
    21→        if detector in STRUCTURAL_MERGE:
    22→            detector = "structural"
    23→        zone = issue.get("zone", "production")
    24→        key = (detector, zone)
    25→        if key not in counts:
    26→            counts[key] = {"total": 0, "fp": 0}
    27→        counts[key]["total"] += 1
    28→        if issue.get("status") == "false_positive":
    29→            counts[key]["fp"] += 1
    30→
    31→    rates: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
    32→    for key, stat in counts.items():
    33→        if stat["total"] >= 5 and stat["fp"] > 0:
    34→            rates[key] = stat["fp"] / stat["total"]
    35→    return rates
    36→
    37→
    38→def _auto_fixer_reminder(actions: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:

    41→        return []
    42→    total = sum(action.get("count", 0) for action in auto_fix_actions)
    43→    if total <= 0:
    44→        return []
    45→    first_cmd = auto_fix_actions[0].get("command", "desloppify autofix <fixer> --dry-run")

    47→        {

    49→            "message": f"{total} issues are auto-fixable. Run `{first_cmd}`.",
    50→            "command": first_cmd,
    51→        }
    52→    ]

106→def collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root: Path) -> list[str]:
   107→    """All exclusion directories as absolute paths, for passing to external tools.
   108→
   109→    Combines DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS (non-glob entries) + get_exclusions() (runtime/config),
   110→    resolves each against *scan_root*. Filters out glob patterns (``*`` in name)
   111→    since most CLI tools want plain directory paths.
   112→    """
   113→    patterns = set()
   114→    for pat in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS:
   115→        if "*" not in pat:
   116→            patterns.add(pat)
   117→    patterns.update(p for p in get_exclusions() if p and "*" not in p)
   118→    return [str(scan_root / p) for p in sorted(patterns) if p]

31→def _detect_unreachable_code(
    32→    filepath: str,
    33→    tree: ast.Module,
    34→    *,
    35→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    36→) -> list[dict]:
    37→    """Flag statements after unconditional return/raise/break/continue.
    38→
    39→    Walks every statement block (function body, if/else body, etc.) and flags
    40→    any statement that follows an unconditional flow-control statement.
    41→    """
    42→    _TERMINAL = (ast.Return, ast.Raise, ast.Break, ast.Continue)
    43→    results: list[dict] = []
    44→
    45→    def _check_block(stmts: list[ast.stmt]):
    46→        for i, stmt in enumerate(stmts):
    47→            if isinstance(stmt, _TERMINAL) and i < len(stmts) - 1:
    48→                next_stmt = stmts[i + 1]
    49→                # Skip flagging string constants (often used as section markers)
    50→                if isinstance(next_stmt, ast.Expr) and isinstance(
    51→                    next_stmt.value, ast.Constant
    52→                ):
    53→                    continue
    54→                results.append(
    55→                    {
    56→                        "file": filepath,
    57→                        "line": next_stmt.lineno,
    58→                        "content": f"unreachable after {type(stmt).__name__.lower()} on line {stmt.lineno}",
    59→                    }
    60→                )
    61→            # Recurse into compound statements
    62→            for attr in ("body", "orelse", "finalbody", "handlers"):
    63→                block = getattr(stmt, attr, None)
    64→                if isinstance(block, list):
    65→                    child_stmts = [s for s in block if isinstance(s, ast.stmt)]
    66→                    if child_stmts:
    67→                        _check_block(child_stmts)
    68→            # ExceptHandler has a body too
    69→            if isinstance(stmt, ast.ExceptHandler):
    70→                _check_block(stmt.body)
    71→
    72→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
    73→        _check_block(node.body)
    74→    return results

77→def _detect_constant_return(
    78→    filepath: str,
    79→    tree: ast.Module,
    80→    *,
    81→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    82→) -> list[dict]:
    83→    """Flag functions that always return the same constant value.
    84→
    85→    Analyzes all return paths — if every return statement returns the same
    86→    literal value (True, False, None, a number, or a string), the function
    87→    likely has dead logic or is a stub masquerading as real code.
    88→    """
    89→    results: list[dict] = []
    90→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
    91→        # Skip tiny functions (stubs/pass-only already caught by dead_function)
    92→        if not hasattr(node, "end_lineno") or not node.end_lineno:
    93→            continue
    94→        loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
    95→        if loc < 4:
    96→            continue
    97→        # Skip decorated functions (properties, abstractmethods, etc.)
    98→        if node.decorator_list:
    99→            continue
   100→
   101→        returns = []
   102→        has_conditional = False
   103→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   104→            if isinstance(child, ast.Return):
   105→                returns.append(child)
   106→            if isinstance(
   107→                child,
   108→                ast.If | ast.For | ast.While | ast.With | ast.Try | ast.ExceptHandler,
   109→            ):
   110→                has_conditional = True
   111→
   112→        # Need at least 2 returns and some conditional logic to be interesting
   113→        if len(returns) < 2 or not has_conditional:
   114→            continue
   115→
   116→        # Extract constant values from all returns
   117→        values = set()
   118→        all_constant = True
   119→        for ret in returns:
   120→            if ret.value is None:
   121→                values.add(repr(None))
   122→            elif isinstance(ret.value, ast.Constant):
   123→                values.add(repr(ret.value.value))
   124→            else:
   125→                all_constant = False
   126→                break
   127→
   128→        if all_constant and len(values) == 1:
   129→            val = next(iter(values))
   130→            # Skip functions that always return None — they're just procedures
   131→            if val == "None":
   132→                continue
   133→            results.append(
   134→                {
   135→                    "file": filepath,
   136→                    "line": node.lineno,
   137→                    "content": f"{node.name}() always returns {val} ({len(returns)} return sites)",
   138→                }
   139→            )
   140→    return results

16→def _compute_fp_rates(issues: dict) -> dict[tuple[str, str], float]:
    17→    """Compute false_positive rate per (detector, zone) from historical issues."""
    18→    counts: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[str, int]] = {}
    19→    for issue in issues.values():
    20→        detector = issue.get("detector", "unknown")
    21→        if detector in STRUCTURAL_MERGE:
    22→            detector = "structural"
    23→        zone = issue.get("zone", "production")
    24→        key = (detector, zone)
    25→        if key not in counts:
    26→            counts[key] = {"total": 0, "fp": 0}
    27→        counts[key]["total"] += 1
    28→        if issue.get("status") == "false_positive":
    29→            counts[key]["fp"] += 1
    30→
    31→    rates: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
    32→    for key, stat in counts.items():
    33→        if stat["total"] >= 5 and stat["fp"] > 0:
    34→            rates[key] = stat["fp"] / stat["total"]
    35→    return rates
